abstract: Coupled hidden Markov models such as the latent structure influence model (LSIM) describe how the sensorimotor rhythms of the two hemispheres evolve and interact during motor imagery, but subject-specific maximum likelihood (ML) estimates are unstable when few trials are available. This paper derives a maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimator for the LSIM whose conjugate prior equals the expected statistics of $λ$ pseudo-trials from a population model fitted to other subjects. The M-step remains in closed form, expectation maximization keeps its monotone ascent, and ML ($λ=0$) and the population model ($λ\to\infty$) are limiting cases. The prior strength was selected on 35 subjects of the PhysioNet EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Dataset and applied unchanged to 70 held-out subjects and to BCI Competition IV-2a. With $λ=1$ the held-out log-likelihood exceeded that of ML in 61 of 70 subjects (Holm-adjusted $p=9.1\times10^{-8}$) and in all 70 subjects with five training trials per class. A prior learned only from the PhysioNet data improved the held-out likelihood of all nine BCI IV-2a subjects at five trials per class and reduced the error of the joint transition matrix by 61%. Decoding accuracy did not improve ($p=0.17$). Cross-subject priors therefore stabilize few-trial dynamic models of motor-imagery EEG, but they do not improve decoding, which in these data relies mainly on structure shared across subjects.

title: Cross-Subject Priors for Maximum a Posteriori Estimation of Latent Structure Influence Models in Motor-Imagery EEG With Few Trials
